passages.quote: In the Edo period the number of seedlings planted was most often expressed as so many to the tsubo. passages.quote: By the Ansei era: 'plant fir about two ken apart lengthwise and crosswise, chestnut four shaku apart, and all other seedlings six shaku apart'. It was also said: 'sugi, fir and chestnut seedlings about six shaku apart, hinoki and others about four or five shaku apart'.
passages.original: 安政年代に至れば「樅は縱横凡貳間置、栗は四尺置、其餘諸苗木は六尺置に植付可申」とされ、或は「杉、樅、栗は苗木六尺置位、檜其外は四・五尺位間を置植付」ともいはれた。

footnotes.assertion: In Hida, rules of the 1850s set the spacing by the kind of tree.One rule set fir about two ken apart each way, chestnut four shaku and other seedlings six; another set sugi, fir and chestnut about six shaku apart and hinoki four or five.

passages.quote: In the hill woods of the Owase-Minamiura district of Kita-Muro county in Kii, where planting of sugi, hinoki and pine is said to have begun about the Genna era, a bakumatsu survey records that about three shaku apart was usual, and that at times 8,000 were planted to the chōbu. In neighboring Hikimoto, 10,000 sugi and hinoki to the chōbu and 7,000 pine were thought proper, and in Aiga village 10,000 sugi and hinoki to the chōbu and 8,000 pine ... in part of the Owase district named above, though it was the same district, sugi and hinoki were set at 800 to the chōbu and pine at 700, an extremely sparse planting.
passages.original: 元和の頃からスギ・ヒノキ・マツの植付が始められたと傳へられる紀伊國北牟婁郡尾鷲南浦地方の山林に於ては、大略三尺間を普通とし、時には壹町歩八千本植付けられたこともあると幕末の調書に記されて居る。またこれに隣接する引本地方ではスギ・ヒノキは一町歩一萬本、マツは七千本を適度となし、相賀村ではスギ・ヒノキは一町歩一萬本、マツは八千本とし、……前記尾鷲地方の一部に於ては、同じ地方でありながらスギ・ヒノキは壹町歩に八百本、マツは七百本と甚だしく疎植をなしたのである。

passages.quote: As the facts above show, whether the planting distance was close or wide depended mainly on whether the timber could be carried out, and it seems that the density was more often constrained by economic conditions than decided on technical grounds.

passages.quote: The method of raising sugi woods in coastal districts practiced from the Tenpo era on in Shizukuishi village, Minami-Iwate county, Rikuchū: 'the planting distance is about four or five to seven or eight to a tsubo (six shaku square); but the spacing differs with the site: where wind and spray are fierce, plant thick to hold off wind damage; and where the ground is shut in by cliffs, like a ravine, and warm and close, the trees grow fast, so plant thin and let them grow well'.
passages.original: 尙陸中國南岩手郡雫石村で天保以降に行はれた海岸地方のスギ林仕立法は「植列の距離は凡そ一坪（六尺四方）に四・五本乃至七・八本とす、然れとも地位に依り疎密を異にし、風潮激烈なる地は密に栽植して風害を防くなり、又洞溪の如き山崖四塞して溫鬱の地等は成木速かなるか故、疎に栽植して其成育を盛んになさしむ」

footnotes.assertion: A rule practiced in one Rikuchū village had coastal sugi planted thicker against the wind.A rule for raising sugi in coastal districts, practiced in a village of Rikuchū from the 1830s on, set four or five to seven or eight to the tsubo: thick where the wind and spray were fierce, to hold off wind damage, and thin in a sheltered valley.

passages.quote: In the first month of the year after next, dig them up and move them, one tree to every two paces square. (This tree must grow large; it may not be planted thick.)
passages.original: 後年正月間，斸移之，方兩步一樹。〈此樹須大，不得穊栽。〉

passages.quote: The qiu has no seed, so dig round a large tree and take its suckers to move. Again one to every two paces square, one row to two mu. A row of a hundred and twenty trees, five rows six hundred trees. After ten years, a tree is worth a thousand cash, the firewood besides.
passages.original: 楸既無子，可於大樹四面掘坑取栽移之。亦方兩步一根，兩畝一行。一行百二十樹，五行合六百樹。十年後，一樹千錢，柴在外。

footnotes.assertion: The Qimin Yaoshu sets catalpa and qiu two paces apart each way.Catalpa goes one tree to every two paces square, not thick, because the tree must grow large, and qiu the same, six hundred trees in five rows.

passages.quote: It suits the bend of a hill. Plow it thoroughly three times, scatter the acorns broadcast, and harrow twice ... Once set, it is not moved. At ten years it serves for rafters ... at twenty for house purlins ... the firewood besides. Cut down, it soon sprouts again; tended, it grows back as before.
passages.original: 宜於山阜之曲，三遍熟耕，漫散橡子，即再勞之。……一定不移。十年，中椽，……二十歲，中屋槫，……柴在外。斫去尋生，料理還復。

footnotes.assertion: The Qimin Yaoshu's oak wood was a coppice, cut and left to sprout, with no count of its stems.The oak is sown broadcast on the bend of a hill and never moved; it is cut for rafters at ten years and for purlins at twenty, and once cut it soon sprouts again.
